Always log a message, regardless of the log level.

## Signature

```typescript
always(message?: unknown, ...args: unknown[]): void;
```

## Parameters

## Returns

void

## Remarks

The message is logged even at `silent`<!-- -->, when no other messages are logged.

It is the only method that is written at `silent`<!-- -->, and it has no prefix. Use it for the messages that must be shown at every log level, like the version or the result requested by the user; for the normal output of an application, that `silent` suppresses, use `output()` (see the table of logging methods in the description of the class).

Before a log level is set (the preliminary state), the message is stored in the internal buffer, like all the others, and is written when the level is set; if the level is never set, it is never written.

The message is passed via `console.log()`<!-- -->. An `Error` object is expanded with the full stack trace and the `cause` chain, on several lines, without a prefix (see the description of `error()`<!-- -->).

## Example


```javascript
log.always(version)
```
